page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.4xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor built on the ARMv9 arm64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz, with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and network connectivity is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth managed by the Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8gd.4xlarge demonstrates top-tier memory performance, with its Passmark memory score placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Large-block uncached memory bandwidth is strong, reaching 296.76 GB/sec for read operations and 130.55 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core performance also rank in the top 25%. However, the server exhibits performance trade-offs in large language model inference tasks, where text generation speeds for small and large models fall into the bottom 10% of benchmarks.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the r8gd.4xlarge is driven by its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and the inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage, which reduces the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput workloads. This hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, and data processing tasks such as multi-threaded decompression. It is less suited for heavy machine learning inference workloads due to its lower benchmarked token generation speeds.
